images.title: Times as heavy: six loads and nine parts
images.purpose: Show that a load 6 times as heavy as 3,000 kg is found by multiplying, and that a small load is found by dividing 450 kg into 9 equal parts.
images.composition: A row of six equal blocks with their total, and one long bar cut into nine equal parts with the part's weight.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP BAR: six equal rounded rectangles, each 170 by 90 px (gaps of 20 px), filled teal #0072B2 with a 3 px dark outline, left edges at x 150, 340, 530, 720, 910, 1100 and y 170 to 260, each holding the text 3,000 kg (32 px, bold, white). A thin grey #6B7280 bracket under the six at y 290 from x 150 to x 1270 with the text 6 times 3,000 kg = 18,000 kg centred under it at y 340 (40 px, bold, dark #1F2937). BOTTOM BAR: one long rounded rectangle 1130 by 90 px at x 150 to 1280, y 480 to 570, outline dark #1F2937, filled very pale grey #F3F4F6, cut by 8 thin vertical lines (3 px) into 9 equal parts each about 125 px wide, each part holding the text 50 kg (30 px, bold, teal). Above the bar, centred at y 440, the text 450 kg (40 px, bold, dark). Under the bar at y 640 the text 450 ÷ 9 = 50 kg (40 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of blocks that differs from 6 in the top bar or 9 parts in the bottom bar
any weight other than 3,000 kg, 18,000 kg, 450 kg and 50 kg
images.takeaway: n times as heavy: multiply to go up, and divide to come back.
images.description: Six blocks of 3,000 kg making 18,000 kg, and a bar of 450 kg cut into nine parts of 50 kg.
images.context: Concept image for Times as Heavy. It follows the idea of one weight being a number of times another in your maths book and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Count the blocks with the student, then count the parts. The slip to watch: adding 6 to the weight instead of taking 6 times.

image_decisions.why: Equal blocks and equal parts show the multiplication and the division as the same relation.
